profile_text.body:
The AI Now Institute is a nonprofit founded in 2017 and headquartered in New York, NY. On its website, the institute describes its work as challenging and reimagining the current trajectory for AI. It publishes an annual report that, in its words, maps the state of play with the AI market, interrogates the industry's key sources of power, and provides an actionable strategy to reclaim public agency over the future of AI.

The institute does not list any products. Its public commentary includes statements from Heidy Khlaaf, its chief AI scientist and a former OpenAI safety engineer, and Sarah Myers West, co-executive director. Khlaaf has said that ordinary security engineering would have stopped the OpenAI hack short of reaching Hugging Face's data, and that scientific claims require falsifiability. West has discussed whether agentic supreme intelligence is possible and the responsibility companies have in developing AI tools.

No litigation cases are listed for the institute. In New York, the institute appears in law exposure data with 448 entries.
